plan_a_advantages: Includes cross-training for recovery and varied stimulus.
Focuses on building aerobic consistency, a foundational element for speed.
plan_b_advantages: More specific focus on running form and cadence.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a greater volume of easy running, totaling 244 minutes over seven days, which is crucial for building a solid aerobic base. Plan B, while including some trail running, has a lower overall volume (260 minutes) and relies more on shorter, form-focused runs, which won't significantly contribute to speed development. Furthermore, Plan A includes a cross-training session, providing a valuable opportunity to maintain fitness without the impact of trail running, aiding recovery and preventing overuse injuries.
